meta.subtitle: VYJUVEK keeps compounding at a 95% gross margin; the fourth-quarter IOLITE readout decides whether the pipeline earns a premium multiple

analystCommentary:
Krystal Biotech is a one-product commercial company that already earns like a mature franchise. VYJUVEK brought in $119.2M in Q2'26, {+ up 24% +} year over year, at a 95% gross margin, and quarterly net income was $54.8M. At $322.28 the stock trades on 40.4x trailing earnings and ~34.6x FY27E consensus EPS, a demanding but not stretched price for that profit stream.

We rate the shares BUY with a $340–$400 target range. The Base case assumes the Street's FY27E numbers arrive and the market keeps paying today's trailing multiple on them; it does not need a pipeline win. The upside beyond that sits with the KB803 IOLITE top-line readout, guided for 4Q 2026, and with the Italy and Spain launches the company expects before year end.

The counter-case is concentration. VYJUVEK is the whole revenue line, Q2'26 growth ran below the pace consensus needs for FY26, and two registrational starts the April 2026 proxy pointed to for later in 2026 are now guided to 2027. Our Bear case, in which earnings stall near FY26E levels, sits below the Street's low target.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Krystal Biotech, Inc. is a Pittsburgh-based, commercial-stage genetic medicines company built on an engineered HSV-1 vector platform. Its only commercial product, VYJUVEK, is a topical, redosable gene therapy for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (DEB), approved in the United States, the EU, Japan and, since May 2026, the UK. The company reports a single segment, and VYJUVEK has generated $965.9M in cumulative net product revenue since its 2023 U.S. launch.

The pipeline uses the same vector across the eye (KB803, KB801), lung (KB407, KB408, inhaled KB707), skin (KB111) and aesthetics (KB304). Two programs, KB803 and KB801, are in studies the company calls registrational. Nothing in the pipeline is yet approved, so today's earnings are VYJUVEK's earnings.

thesis.body:
The core of the case is that VYJUVEK alone already supports most of the share price. Q2'26 revenue grew {+ 24% +} with an operating margin of 49%, the company held $1.1 billion in cash and investments at June 30, 2026, and the Street's FY27E EPS of $9.32 puts the stock at ~34.6x forward earnings.

We think that price leaves room for a Base case built on consensus delivery alone, with the pipeline as the swing factor. The counter-case is that growth is slowing from FY25's {+ +33.9% +} and that the next leg depends on European pricing and an eye-drop trial with 16 patients. That balance supports a BUY, not a STRONG BUY.

catalysts: KB803 IOLITE top-line results, guided for 4Q 2026; see Growth.
VYJUVEK launches in Italy and Spain, which the company expects before year end; see Growth.
Completion of EMERALD-1 enrollment for KB801 and FDA alignment on the KB407 registrational design, both guided for late 2026.
risks: Single-product dependence: the 2025 10-K says near-term prospects are substantially dependent on VYJUVEK's commercial success.
Growth deceleration against a consensus that needs a stronger second half; see Financials.
Pipeline timelines have already slipped once this year; see Management.

financials.incomeCommentary:
The income statement has turned from losses to high margins in three years. Diluted EPS went from a loss of $5.49 per share in FY22 to positive results of 0.39 in FY23, 3.00 in FY24 and 6.84 in FY25, while operating margin moved from a negative 216.2% in FY23 to 22.6% in FY24 and 41.5% in FY25. FY25 revenue was $389.1M, {+ up 33.9% +}.

The Q2'26 quarter kept the margin story intact. Product revenue was $119.2M against $96.0M a year earlier, cost of goods sold fell to $6.4M from $7.2M, and gross margin was 95%. R&D was flat at $14.5M against $14.4M, while SG&A rose to $39.9M from $35.1M, so operating leverage came mainly from the revenue line. Diluted EPS was $1.79 against $1.29.

Two cautions. First, growth is slowing: Q2'26 revenue rose {+ 24.1% +}, below the FY25 pace and below the ~31% growth embedded in the FY26E consensus of $511.1M. First-half revenue was $235.6M, so consensus implies second-half revenue well above that figure; Italy and Spain launches would help, but German and French pricing remains unsettled. Second, TTM net margin of 54.8% sits above the 44.9% operating margin; the facts here do not say why, so we do not treat the gap as recurring. Consensus EPS basis is unstated, while reported EPS is GAAP and includes stock-based compensation of $11.7M in Q2'26 SG&A alone.
financials.balanceCommentary:
The balance sheet is a strength. Cash and short-term investments rose in each year from FY22 to FY25, reaching $0.8B at FY25, and the Q2'26 press release reports $1.1 billion in cash and investments at June 30, 2026. Total equity reached $1.2B in FY25. The vendor table shows no debt figures ("—"), which we treat as missing data rather than as zero; the excerpts in Context do not describe any borrowing either.

Liquidity is ample: the TTM current ratio is 8.32, down from levels above 13 in FY21–FY23 as the business scaled, but still high. The practical read is that Krystal can fund every disclosed program, including the registrational starts guided for 2027, without new equity. The counter-point is that a large idle cash balance only helps holders if it is spent well; capital allocation is discussed under Management.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Cash generation now tracks earnings. FY25 free cash flow was $188.9M, a 48.5% FCF margin, up from 41.0% in FY24, with capital expenditure of $12M. Operating cash flow and free cash flow have both been positive only since FY24; FY21–FY23 were cash-consuming years.

At today's price the FCF yield is 2.7%, which is thin for a single-product company and means most of the valuation rests on growth rather than current cash returns. The company pays no dividend and the vendor shows no repurchases. Management's FY 2026 guidance for non-GAAP R&D and SG&A combined is $175.0 - $195.0 million, excluding stock-based compensation, which the company says it cannot estimate. Spending within that range against a revenue base heading toward consensus would keep free cash flow rising; a step-up in registrational spending in 2027 is the main reason it might not.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
On trailing numbers the stock is priced at 40.4x earnings, 43.7x EV/EBITDA and 21.7x sales. On forward numbers the vendor gives two figures that disagree: ~34.6x on FY27E EPS in the snapshot and 41.0x on an NTM basis in the multiples table. We use the FY27E figure because it maps directly to the consensus EPS of $9.32 our scenarios use, and note that the NTM figure reads closer to the trailing multiple. The consensus EPS basis is unstated, so we do not call these forward multiples GAAP-based.

No peer multiples are available, so the read is absolute. A multiple near 40x trailing for a business with a 95% gross margin and roughly half of revenue converting to free cash flow is not extreme, but it leaves no room for VYJUVEK growth to stall. The Street's consensus target of $392.11 and median of $400.00 sit above our Base, and its $284.00 low sits above our Bear.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: IOLITE reads out positively in 4Q 2026, Italy and Spain launch on schedule, and EMERALD-1 completes enrollment. The market starts paying for a second product, and the stock reaches the Street's high target of $474.00.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: VYJUVEK delivers consensus FY27E EPS of $9.32 and the market keeps paying today's 40.4x trailing P/E once those earnings become the trailing figure. Pipeline readouts are mixed and add little to value.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: IOLITE misses and European pricing comes in below expectations, so earnings stall near FY26E EPS of $7.87 instead of compounding into FY27, and the stock is valued at the current ~34.6x forward multiple on that lower base.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
The scenarios are anchored so a reader can check them: Base applies the trailing P/E to FY27E consensus EPS, Bear applies the forward P/E to FY26E consensus EPS, and Bull uses the Street's high target.

We weight Base at 50% and Bull and Bear at 25% each. The weighting is symmetric because the two tails turn on the same events, chiefly IOLITE and the European pricing outcomes, which tend to push in one direction or the other rather than both at once. The probability-weighted fair value lands above Base because the Bull upside is wider than the Bear downside, and the expected upside clears the BUY threshold with a Bear downside of about the same size.

The main sensitivity is the multiple. The Bear case keeps a forward multiple in the mid-30s; if the market instead re-rated a single-product company with slowing growth well below that, the downside would be wider than modeled.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Krystal reports one segment, and all FY25 revenue of $389.1M came from VYJUVEK net product sales. The company sells directly in the United States, major European markets and Japan, and is building a specialty distributor network elsewhere. The vendor data carry no geographic split, so we do not quote one. Pricing is settled in Japan, still under negotiation in Germany and France, and under discussion in Italy, Spain and the UK, per the Q2'26 10-Q.

moatFactors.name: First corrective therapy in DEB
moatFactors.body: The Q2'26 10-Q describes VYJUVEK as "the first and only corrective medicine approved by the FDA for the treatment of both recessive and dominant subtypes of DEB," and says it is "the first and only corrective therapy approved for the treatment of DEB" in Japan, the EU and the UK. A September 2025 U.S. label update extended eligibility to patients from birth and allowed home application by patients or caregivers. The limit is that this protects one indication in a rare disease, not a broad franchise.

moatFactors.name: Biologic exclusivity
moatFactors.body: The 2025 10-K describes a 12-year period before a biosimilar approval can take effect after a reference product's first FDA licensure. The same risk factor warns that a competitor can still win approval during that window with its own full BLA, that the period could be shortened by congressional action, and that recent FDA draft guidance could lower the burden for biosimilars. We treat exclusivity as real but not absolute.

moatFactors.name: Commercial and manufacturing footprint
moatFactors.body: The company runs two in-house, commercial scale CGMP manufacturing facilities and, per the Q2'26 press release, has secured over 730 reimbursement approvals and over 640 unique prescribers for VYJUVEK. That base takes time for a newcomer to rebuild. It is still a footprint in one disease, and it does not transfer automatically to the eye, lung or skin programs.

moatFactors.name: Vector platform
moatFactors.body: In October 2025 the FDA granted platform technology designation to the HSV-1 vector used in KB801, which the 10-Q says affords development and manufacturing efficiencies. This is a potential advantage across the pipeline, but it has not yet produced a second approval.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. VYJUVEK's position in DEB looks durable over the next several years, supported by its approval status in four jurisdictions, the expanded U.S. label and the reimbursement base. The moat does not extend beyond one rare-disease indication today, and the 10-K itself flags that full-BLA competitors and changes to biosimilar policy could erode exclusivity. A positive IOLITE readout would extend the franchise within DEB rather than widen it into new diseases; a KB801 approval would be an early test of whether the platform designation turns into a broader advantage. What to watch: any competing BLA in DEB and the outcome of European pricing.

points: VYJUVEK geographic expansion: launched in Germany in August 2025 and in France and Japan in October 2025, approved in the UK in May 2026, with Italy and Spain launches expected before year end and marketing authorization applications for Switzerland and Australia planned for 2H 2026. The counter-case is pricing: German negotiations run until at least 2H 2026 and French ones into 2027, so European revenue per patient is not yet settled.

U.S. depth: the September 2025 label update opened treatment from birth and home application, and the company reports growing use of VYJUVEK as a lifelong wound management therapy. The facts do not split U.S. from international revenue, so we cannot confirm how much of the {+ 24% +} Q2'26 growth came from the U.S.

KB803 (IOLITE): a registrational, placebo-controlled crossover study in DEB patients with corneal abrasions, fully enrolled in April 2026 with 16 patients, top-line results guided for 4Q 2026. The 10-Q says ocular complications are thought to affect over 25% of DEB patients and that no corrective therapy is available. The evidence beyond IOLITE is a single compassionate-use case, so we do not assume a positive readout.

KB801 (EMERALD-1) for neurotrophic keratitis: a registrational study of approximately 60 patients, enrollment guided to complete before year end. This would give Krystal a product outside DEB; recombinant NGF eye drops are already approved for NK, so KB801 would compete on dosing burden rather than enter an empty market.

Later-stage optionality: KB407 in cystic fibrosis (FDA alignment on a registrational design expected in 4Q 2026, study start in 2027), KB111 in Hailey-Hailey disease (registrational start targeted for 2027) and inhaled KB707 in NSCLC (31% ORR with pembrolizumab in a late-line Phase 1/2 cohort, registrational plans in 1H 2027). These are early and contribute little to our Base case.

management.leadership:
Per the April 3, 2026 proxy, the 2025 named executive officers were Krish S. Krishnan, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer; Suma M. Krishnan, Founder and President; and Kathryn A. Romano, Executive Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer. The proxy excerpt carries no tenure or background detail, so we do not add any.

Execution on VYJUVEK has been strong: approvals in four jurisdictions and a profitable launch. Pipeline timing is less reliable. The April 2026 proxy said the company had the potential to initiate registrational programs in cystic fibrosis and Hailey-Hailey disease later in 2026; the August 2026 press release now targets 2027 for both. The documents do not give a reason for the change. We read it as a modest credibility cost, not a red flag, and the 4Q 2026 KB407 FDA alignment is the date to hold management to.
management.capitalAllocation:
Capital so far has gone to R&D, the commercial build-out and in-house manufacturing; the vendor shows no buybacks and no dividends. The FY 2026 non-GAAP opex guidance in Financials keeps spending disciplined relative to revenue.

The open question is the use of a cash balance that keeps growing. Management is funding several registrational programs and a separate aesthetics subsidiary, Jeune Aesthetics, which plans a Phase 2 KB304 study in 2027. Aesthetics is a different market from rare disease, and the filings in Context do not explain its expected economics. We would prefer to see cash spent on the eye and lung programs first; any large acquisition or a step-up in aesthetics spending would weaken the case.
management.governance:
Per the April 3, 2026 proxy, the Board determined that six current directors (Messrs. Gangolli, Janney and Rossi, Drs. Mason and Sutherland, and Ms. Mazzacco) and former director Mr. Ganorkar are independent under Nasdaq standards. The excerpt does not give the total board size, so we cannot state the independent share. The CEO also chairs the board, and the excerpt does not mention a lead independent director, which leaves less independent counterweight to management.

The Audit Committee must review and approve related-party transactions above $120,000, per the proxy's written policy; the excerpt discloses no specific transactions. Overall governance looks standard for a founder-led biotech, with the combined Chairman and CEO role the main point to monitor.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy excerpt in Context does not include the beneficial ownership table, so we cannot state what share of Krystal the executives, the founder or any 5% holder owns. Such holder figures typically come from the holders' own 13G filings, and none were captured. Without that data we make no claim about insider control; the governance view above rests on board structure alone.

idiosyncratic: Product concentration: VYJUVEK is Krystal's sole commercial product, and the 2025 10-K states that near-term prospects and future growth are substantially dependent on its commercial success. Any safety signal, supply interruption or slowdown in U.S. demand would hit the entire revenue line. Watch quarterly VYJUVEK revenue growth against the Q2'26 pace.

European pricing: the company is selling in Germany and France ahead of final prices, with negotiations running until at least 2H 2026 in Germany and into 2027 in France. A final price below the launch level could require lower future revenue per patient. Watch the German outcome and the Italy and Spain launch prices.

IOLITE readout: a small crossover trial in a rare population carries real binary risk, and the company changed the KB803 dosing schedule after the study began. A miss would remove the most visible near-term extension of the DEB franchise. Watch the 4Q 2026 top-line release, including the primary endpoint versus placebo.

Biosimilar and competitor entry: the 2025 10-K warns that a rival can win approval with its own BLA during the 12-year exclusivity window and that recent FDA draft guidance could accelerate biosimilar competition. Entry would pressure price and share in DEB. Watch FDA guidance finalization and any competing DEB filings.

Pipeline slippage: two registrational starts have moved from 2026 to 2027, and KB408 interim results are not due until 2027. Further delays would push any second revenue stream out and weaken the Bull case. Watch the 4Q 2026 KB407 FDA alignment and the 2027 study starts.
risks.systemic: The broader risks are those of any U.S. rare-disease drug company: pricing and reimbursement policy, FDA policy on biologics and gene therapies, and changes to biosimilar exclusivity, all of which the 2025 10-K names. The stock's 52-week range of $179.16 – $382.54 shows how far sentiment can swing. With no debt shown in the vendor data and $1.1 billion in cash and investments, rate and credit conditions matter mainly through the multiple the market will pay, not through funding.

body: We rate Krystal Biotech BUY with a $340–$400 target range against a $322.28 price. VYJUVEK's earnings, if they reach FY27E consensus, support the Base case without any pipeline contribution, and the cash balance funds every disclosed program.

What would change the call: a weak IOLITE readout combined with Q3'26 or Q4'26 VYJUVEK growth below the Q2'26 pace would move us toward HOLD, because it would point to the Bear path of stalled earnings. A positive IOLITE result with clean European pricing would move fair value toward the Bull case.
